name: 1st Grade Mathematics
description: Twelve units covering every Common Core / Massachusetts Grade 1 mathematics standard (20 leaf standards plus the 1.NBT.B.2 statement and its parts a, b and c), 47 skills with observable learning targets.

source.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Grade 1 (identical codes in the Massachusetts 2017 Mathematics Curriculum Framework)
source.note: Replaces the earlier scope-and-sequence outline (8 units, 93 skills), as was done for Grade 2. Skill source of truth: tools/grade1-authoring/outline.py.

standards.1.OA.A.1: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
standards.1.OA.A.2: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
standards.1.OA.B.3: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. (Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12.)
standards.1.OA.B.4: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 − 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.
standards.1.OA.C.5: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).
standards.1.OA.C.6: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten; decomposing a number leading to a ten; using the relationship between addition and subtraction; and creating equivalent but easier or known sums.
standards.1.OA.D.7: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
standards.1.OA.D.8: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.1.NBT.A.1: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
standards.1.NBT.B.2: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.
standards.1.NBT.B.2.a: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a “ten.”
standards.1.NBT.B.2.b: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
standards.1.NBT.B.2.c: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).
standards.1.NBT.B.3: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.
standards.1.NBT.C.4: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.
standards.1.NBT.C.5: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.
standards.1.NBT.C.6: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
standards.1.MD.A.1: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
standards.1.MD.A.2: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.
standards.1.MD.B.3: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.
standards.1.MD.C.4: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.
standards.1.G.A.1: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.
standards.1.G.A.2: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
standards.1.G.A.3: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

units.name: Counting and Numbers to 120
units.description: Counting objects, counting on from any number to 120, reading and writing numerals, and counting on or back to add and subtract.
skills: Counting On and Back to Add and Subtract
targets: I can count a group of objects and write the number.
I can count forward from any number up to 120 and say what number comes next.
I can read and write numbers to 120 and match number words to numerals.
I can count on to add and count back to subtract.

units.name: Addition and Subtraction within 10
units.description: Adding and subtracting within 10 with ten frames and counters, pairs that make ten, and fluent facts within 10.
targets: I can add two numbers with a sum up to 10.
I can subtract numbers within 10.
I can find the number that goes with another number to make 10.
I can break a number up to 10 into two parts and find a missing part.

units.name: Addition and Subtraction within 20
units.description: Strategies for adding and subtracting within 20: make a ten, doubles, adding three numbers, and related facts.
skills: Adding in Any Order and Adding Three Numbers
targets: I can add within 20 by making a ten, using doubles, or counting on.
I can subtract within 20 by counting back, going back to 10, or thinking addition.
I can change the order of addends and add three numbers by finding a ten first.
I can use an addition fact to solve a related subtraction fact.

units.name: The Equal Sign and Missing Numbers
units.description: Understanding the equal sign as “the same as,” true and false equations, and finding unknown numbers.
targets: I can tell whether an equation is true or false by checking that both sides are the same amount.
I can find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation.
I can find a number that makes both sides of an equation the same, such as 6 + 4 = 5 + ___.

units.name: Word Problems within 20
units.description: Add to, take from, put together, take apart and compare stories within 20, with unknowns in all positions and three addends.
skills: Add To and Take From Stories
Put Together and Take Apart Stories
Stories with a Missing Start or Change
targets: I can solve stories where some are added or taken away.
I can solve stories about two parts and a total.
I can solve stories that ask how many more or how many fewer.
I can solve stories where the start or the change is unknown.
I can solve stories that add three numbers with a total up to 20.

units.name: Tens and Ones
units.description: A ten as ten ones, teen numbers as a ten and some ones, decade numbers, and tens and ones in two-digit numbers.
skills: Tens and Ones in Two-Digit Numbers
targets: I can make a ten from ten ones and tell how many tens and ones are in a group.
I can show a number from 11 to 19 as one ten and some ones.
I can count by tens and tell how many tens are in 10, 20, 30, … 90.
I can tell how many tens and ones are in a two-digit number and show it with blocks.

units.name: Comparing Two-Digit Numbers
units.description: Comparing two-digit numbers by tens and ones and recording comparisons with >, = and <.
targets: I can tell which of two numbers is greater by comparing the tens first, then the ones.
I can write a comparison using the symbols >, =, and <.
I can find numbers that make a comparison true and explain my thinking.

units.name: Adding and Subtracting within 100
units.description: Ten more and ten less, adding and subtracting tens, adding a one-digit number, and making a new ten.
skills: Adding a Two-Digit and a One-Digit Number
targets: I can find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number without counting by ones.
I can add tens to a two-digit number and subtract tens from tens.
I can add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when no new ten is made.
I can add a one-digit number to a two-digit number when the ones make a new ten.
I can add two two-digit numbers within 100 by adding tens and tens and ones and ones.

units.name: Measuring Length
units.description: Ordering objects by length, comparing indirectly, and measuring with same-size units laid end to end.
targets: I can compare two lengths and put three objects in order from shortest to longest.
I can use a third object to compare two lengths.
I can measure a length by counting same-size units laid end to end.
I can tell when a measurement is wrong because of gaps, overlaps, or units of different sizes.

units.name: Telling Time
units.description: Telling and writing time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
targets: I can tell and write time to the hour on analog and digital clocks.
I can tell and write time to the half hour on analog and digital clocks.
I can match analog and digital times and tell what time it will be one hour or half an hour later.

units.name: Organizing and Reading Data
units.description: Sorting, tally charts, picture graphs and tables with up to three categories, and answering questions about data.
targets: I can sort objects into up to three groups and use tally marks to show how many.
I can read how many are in each category of a picture graph, tally chart, or table.
I can find the total and tell how many more or fewer are in one category than another.

units.name: Shapes and Equal Shares
units.description: Defining attributes of shapes, naming 2-D and 3-D shapes, composing shapes, and halves and fourths.
targets: I can tell which attributes make a shape what it is (closed, number of sides and corners) and which do not (color, size, position).
I can name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and rectangular prisms.
I can put shapes together to make new shapes and tell how many shapes I used.
I can split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal shares and name halves, fourths, and quarters.
I can describe a whole as two halves or four fourths and explain that more equal shares are smaller shares.
